statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail 25% crosses one point into the block band after NQ futures set a fresh session low at 30,407.25, with the US 10-year at 5.14%, Japan's 10-year at a 1996 high, VIX up 6.7% and Brent up 2.2%.
recommendation: Tail has moved from the top of the watch band into the block band, so the deterministic mapping yields BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES rather than WATCH. The change reflects observed extension to a new session low rather than a new catalyst. The evidence-based danger window runs from the current hour to 16:00 UTC, covering the 12:30 UTC claims release, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the afternoon data sequence, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would confirm mean-reversion failure and a genuine two-way open would argue for a lower Tail.
headline: NQ futures set a fresh session low as US and Japanese yields hold multi-decade highs
body: NQ futures trade near 30,430, down about 1.1%, after printing a fresh session low at 30,407.25 and extending the decline from the 30,813.00 overnight high to roughly 1.3%. Two independent quote sources agree on the level and on the 30,407.25 low, which is the single most important change since the previous assessment: the prior hour's 30,479.00 low has been taken out, so the overnight pattern is now repeated extension after a failed retracement rather than a stabilising drift. The driver remains duration rather than equity-specific news. The US 10-year yield holds about 5.143%, its highest since July 2007, with the 2-year near 4.91%, its highest since 2023. Japan's 10-year has added roughly 9.5 basis points to about 3.084%, the highest since August 1996, as the global rout deepened on the reopening after Silver Week. VIX has risen to 16.20 from a 15.18 close, a gain of 6.7%, and has set a 16.36 session high. Energy is reinforcing the inflation channel, with Brent at $105.35, up 2.2%, and WTI at $93.79, up 1.8%, as US-Iran talks show scant evidence of progress. The policy backdrop is hawkish: the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points for the first time since 2023, and futures traders are pricing two further quarter-point increases by year end, so an already extended bond move is being reinforced rather than faded. Four independent amplifiers are therefore aligned at once - yields at a cycle high, oil extending, implied volatility rising and NQ holding within roughly 25 points of a session extreme it has just re-set. Two considerations keep this short of a more severe reading. The cumulative decline is about 1.3% over roughly nine hours, which is an orderly grind rather than violent repricing, and the move is occurring in the pre-cash session where thinner liquidity carries less structural information. Yesterday's cash session also traded a 30,353.88-30,706.23 range in the Nasdaq-100 and closed at 30,470.29, well above its low, so retracement was still being rewarded as recently as the previous close. Tail therefore steps one point across the block threshold rather than further into it, while Stress carries the multi-decade-high yield backdrop and the open energy channel. Shared Finviz context was read at the start of this run but was 157 minutes old and marked partial, so it was treated as stale under the supporting-evidence contract and no part of it was used as evidence. The structural checkpoints ahead are the 12:00 UTC Fed Barkin speech, the 12:30 UTC jobless claims release, the 13:30 UTC US cash open, new home sales at 14:00 UTC and the Kansas City Fed index at 15:00 UTC.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 12-15% through the European and early US hours of Sep 23 in a normal-to-mixed regime, then printed 25% for the 14:00 UTC hour as the post-PMI bond leg developed. It held 20-24% through the US afternoon and into the Asian session, eased to 17-19% between 01:00 and 03:00 UTC, printed 22% at 04:00 UTC on a brief trend-down read, and closed the window at 21% and then 24% for the 07:00 and 08:00 UTC hours as the duration move re-accelerated. Stress was the more persistent signal, rising from the mid-30s to 57% at 18:00 UTC, easing to around 50% overnight and returning to 57% for the final slot. Confidence stayed in the 84-88% band throughout.
outlookSummary: The published path holds Tail in the block band at 25-27% from the current hour through 15:00 UTC, peaking across the 13:00 and 14:00 UTC claims-reaction and cash-open sequence, which defines the evidence-based danger window. It steps back to the watch band at 24% from 16:00 UTC, decays through the US afternoon and evening to 19-20% by the Asian session, and drifts back to 20-21% across the following European hours as the amplifier stack is assumed to unwind slowly. Stress follows the same shape at a higher level, peaking at 61%, because the multi-decade-high yield level and the open energy channel persist regardless of intraday structure. Confidence decays from 85% to 75% as the current price-path evidence ages across the window. The forecast assumes the rate-repricing regime stays unresolved but that price discovery remains orderly. Observed opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would argue for a higher Tail than published, while a cooling bond market or a genuine two-way cash open would argue for a lower one.
